name: Tauber Bridge, Rothenburg ob der Tauber
wikipediaTitle: Tauber Bridge, Rothenburg ob der Tauber
facts: The Tauber Bridge, a double arch marvel from around 1330, once carried a vital trade route linking Augsburg to Würzburg across the Tauber Valley.
After four upper arches collapsed in 1790, the bridge was renovated in 1791, only to be blown up by German troops in 1945 and rebuilt in 1955, reopening on 10 November 1956.
With a 4.0‑metre roadway and a 1.0‑metre footpath, the Tauber Bridge remains a narrow but iconic crossing, straddling the southwestern valley side below Rothenburg ob der Tauber.
